classification.difficultyReason: Find linear factors of expanded quartics using root testing and division, identify repeated roots, and translate the resulting signs into intervals while handling isolated zeros and strict endpoints.

content.prompt: By factorising first, solve the following.

answer.short:
$-4<x<-3$ or $-2<x<1$.

Factorise and select the regions below the $x$-axis; exclude all roots.
answer.worked:
The factor theorem gives roots $-4,-3,-2,1$.
$$\begin{align*}x^4+8x^3+17x^2-2x-24&=(x^2+7x+12)(x^2+x-2)\\x^4+8x^3+17x^2-2x-24&=(x+4)(x+3)(x+2)(x-1).\end{align*}$$
The leading coefficient is positive, so both ends of the graph point upwards. Each root is simple, so the graph crosses the axis at each root. It is below the axis between $-4$ and $-3$, and between $-2$ and $1$. The inequality is strict, so the roots are excluded.
$$-4<x<-3\quad\text{or}\quad-2<x<1.$$

answer.short:
$x\le-3$ or $-2\le x\le1$ or $x\ge5$.

Factorise and select the regions on or above the $x$-axis.
answer.worked:
The factor theorem gives roots $-3,-2,1,5$.
$$\begin{align*}x^4-x^3-19x^2-11x+30&=(x^2+5x+6)(x^2-6x+5)\\x^4-x^3-19x^2-11x+30&=(x+3)(x+2)(x-1)(x-5).\end{align*}$$
Both ends of the graph point upwards. All four roots are simple, so the graph crosses the axis at each one. It is above the axis to the left of $-3$, between $-2$ and $1$, and to the right of $5$. Include all roots because equality is permitted.
$$x\le-3\quad\text{or}\quad-2\le x\le1\quad\text{or}\quad x\ge5.$$

answer.short:
$-3<x<-2$ or $-2<x<1$.

The double root at $-2$ is excluded because the inequality is strict.
answer.worked:
The factor theorem gives roots $-3,-2,1$; division leaves a second factor of $x+2$.
$$\begin{align*}x^4+6x^3+9x^2-4x-12&=(x^2+2x-3)(x^2+4x+4)\\x^4+6x^3+9x^2-4x-12&=(x+3)(x-1)(x+2)^2.\end{align*}$$
Both ends of the graph point upwards. It crosses at $-3$ and $1$ and touches the axis at the double root $-2$. Between $-3$ and $1$ it is below the axis except at $-2$, where it equals zero. Exclude every root.
$$-3<x<-2\quad\text{or}\quad-2<x<1.$$

answer.short:
$-1\le x\le2$ or $x=3$.

Include the isolated double root at $3$ because equality is permitted.
answer.worked:
The factor theorem gives roots $-1,2,3$; division leaves a second factor of $x-3$.
$$\begin{align*}x^4-7x^3+13x^2+3x-18&=(x^2-x-2)(x^2-6x+9)\\x^4-7x^3+13x^2+3x-18&=(x+1)(x-2)(x-3)^2.\end{align*}$$
Both ends of the graph point upwards. It crosses at $-1$ and $2$, and touches the axis at $3$. The graph is below the axis between $-1$ and $2$. Include the endpoints and the isolated zero at $3$.
$$-1\le x\le2\quad\text{or}\quad x=3.$$

answer.short:
$x<-3$ or $-3<x<1$ or $x>2$.

Exclude the double root at $-3$ as well as the simple roots.
answer.worked:
The factor theorem gives roots $-3,1,2$; division leaves a second factor of $x+3$.
$$\begin{align*}x^4+3x^3-7x^2-15x+18&=(x^2+6x+9)(x^2-3x+2)\\x^4+3x^3-7x^2-15x+18&=(x+3)^2(x-1)(x-2).\end{align*}$$
Both ends of the graph point upwards. It touches the axis at $-3$ and crosses at $1$ and $2$. It is above the axis for $x<1$, apart from the zero at $-3$, and for $x>2$. Exclude all roots because the inequality is strict.
$$x<-3\quad\text{or}\quad-3<x<1\quad\text{or}\quad x>2.$$

answer.short:
$x\le-1$ or $x=2$ or $x\ge3$.

Include the isolated double root at $2$ because equality is permitted.
answer.worked:
The factor theorem gives roots $-1,2,3$; division leaves a second factor of $x-2$.
$$\begin{align*}x^4-6x^3+9x^2+4x-12&=(x^2-2x-3)(x^2-4x+4)\\x^4-6x^3+9x^2+4x-12&=(x+1)(x-3)(x-2)^2.\end{align*}$$
Both ends of the graph point upwards. It crosses at $-1$ and $3$, and touches the axis at $2$. It is above the axis for $x<-1$ and $x>3$. Include both endpoints and the isolated zero at $2$.
$$x\le-1\quad\text{or}\quad x=2\quad\text{or}\quad x\ge3.$$
